endorsements.quote: New or modified methods enter the catalog only through the same fit‐for‐purpose validation and independent verification, and each study is bound to specific agent versions so that an analysis in progress is never altered silently by a catalog update, while superseded agents are formally deprecated.

Each agent is validated against its method specification before deployment, in keeping with risk‐based practice for computerized systems [ 22 ], by means of a versioned validation test suite of known‐answer cases that the agent must reproduce exactly, with acceptance criteria that are themselves pre‐specified and version‐controlled, so that any change to the model, the method, or the runtime dependencies triggers regression testing against the locked reference.

The depth of validation scales with model risk, understood as the product of an agent's influence on a result and the consequence of that result, in line with the risk‐proportionate approach that regulators are adopting for AI [ 23 ].

The scientist then conducts a methodological audit, verifying the statistical model specification and the exact implementation of the decision rules much as a statistical analysis plan is reviewed before database lock, and an independent AI reviewer separately checks that the generated code faithfully implements the locked specification.
The second requirement is role clarity and accountability.

Translating intent into a structured operational specification is the primary control point, and the work is collaborative: the scientist supplies domain knowledge and judgment, while the LLM articulates loosely framed questions as bounded specifications and surfaces hidden choices.
Each revision is recorded in the same deviations log with who raised it, what changed, and when, so that the scientist's authority to override the agent is unconditional but never silent.
The third requirement is monitoring and lifecycle management.

Because execution outside the LLM and a fixed catalog remove the structural cause of implementation drift, monitoring is not the detection of drift after the fact but the continuing assurance that the controls remain intact, through periodic re‐execution of the validation test suites, comparison of output hashes against the locked references, and alerts on any change to the catalog, a version, or a dependency.
When disagreement surfaces at the reporting stage, the scientist's judgment supersedes the agent's output, and the remedy depends on the type of disagreement.

unlisted_practices: Formally encode and lock analytical intent in a tamper-evident, hashed analysis plan before any analysis is executed, requiring documented amendment and re-lock for any change.

Execute the analysis of record outside the LLM as version-controlled, specification-verified code in a validated environment with pinned code, seeds, and dependencies, so that raw data never enter the model.
Generate code for each analytical objective in a separate fresh LLM session seeded only with the locked plan and data dictionary to prevent context drift.
Maintain a forbidden-operations registry barring unplanned comparisons and inferential summaries before the plan is locked.
Report every pre-specified objective regardless of statistical significance and keep a mandatory timestamped deviations log of departures from the locked plan.
Use only a governed library of documented, validated agents for recurring studies, separating a version-controlled method layer from a deployment layer.
Obtain cross-functional consensus on the analysis plan before locking it, and review disagreement log entries on a fixed cadence feeding formally re-validated changes.
Ensure no AI component is both author and sole reviewer of analytical work, with an independent reviewer checking narrative against the numbers.
Require deterministic execution outside the LLM even for low-stakes analytical agents.

screen.reason: This is a position paper proposing a compliance-by-design governance framework and architectural principles (e.g., execution firewall, governed agent library) for integrating AI/LLMs into quantitative analysis in clinical and translational research.
